label: sponge-associated environment
definition: An animal-associated environment which is determined by a sponge.

Definition drafted from the record's deep-research report under research/habitats/ and read against it; the report's proposed wording, genus and near-miss table are the evidence. Parented to the aquatic-invertebrate term rather than to animal-associated environment, which the report identified as the more specific existing genus. Genus moved from ENVO:01001176 'environment associated with an aquatic invertebrate' to ENVO:01001002 (#210), with the whole aquatic-invertebrate host family rather than record by record - #210 was filed over three records and the genus is actually held by five, so fixing only the three would have rebuilt the same split it reports. Both terms are true of the concept, so this chooses between two true genera on what each drags in: ENVO asserts ENVO:01001176 under ENVO:01001002 AND ENVO:01001055 'environment associated with an animal part or small animal', so the tighter genus makes every descendant inherit a size-and-partonomy restriction that is false of a whole adult sponge, ascidian, oyster, giant clam or sea urchin. ENVO's own modelling is the decisive evidence: ENVO:01001179 'cnidarian-associated environment' - the closest analogue, a taxon-scoped class over aquatic invertebrates - is asserted under ENVO:01001002 ALONE, and ENVO:01001176 has no children in the slice at all. Not carried as an xref: it is genuinely broader, so recording it would re-import the ancestry this declines.

label: inland saline or alkaline aquatic environment
definition: An aquatic environment which is determined by an inland water body whose water is substantially more saline than fresh water, substantially more alkaline than circumneutral water, or both.
editors note: Requested by HabitatMech. Attested by BACDIVE, GOLD with 158 upstream assertions across 2 source concept(s): Non-marine-Saline-and-Alkaline; Environmental > Aquatic > Non-marine Saline and Alkaline. Definition curated from the committed deep-research report for this record (#110, #185). The “or both” wording preserves GOLD's disjunctive hierarchy instead of claiming every child is simultaneously saline and alkaline. “Inland” is preferred to “non-marine” because marine-derived inland brines can remain geographically inland, while “athalassohaline” is not an exact synonym because it classifies water by ionic composition rather than location. Parent replacement is intentional: GOLD's inherited aquatic-biome edge is false for the node's operated-setting descendants, whereas ENVO's aquatic-environment genus covers both natural and engineered water-determined settings. Dropped the exact synonym 'Non-marine-Saline-and-Alkaline' (#213): it is BacDive's label for the concept GOLD spells 'Non-marine Saline and Alkaline', and the two differ only in punctuation. Both source labels survive on the record's source_attestations, where they identify which source said what; as a pair of EXACT synonyms they would read to an ENVO editor as the same string written twice. Found by the guard added for this issue, not by the review that filed it. Scope correction #1415: remove the three saline-only exact aliases because they omit the alkaline-only arm. Preserve the disjunctive definition, aquatic-environment REPLACE mode, reviewed source merge and separate assertion units.
